## Headline characterisation (correlation PCA, 39 slices, n_eff caveat attached)

The three symbolic-capital components **load consistently, moderately and with one shared sign on PC1 (oriented +0.30 / +0.27 / +0.23, ranks 5, 6, 10 of 12), and they are the most tightly clustered group on PC1** — within-symbolic range 0.0735 versus 0.58–0.74 for every other group. They are **co-signed but not co-dominant**: PC1's leading loadings are Copper&Gold (+0.407), Pottery Decoration (+0.382), Pottery Form (−0.353) and Depot (+0.340). On PC2 the trio is nominally **on the same side of zero (all positive) but is effectively absent from it**: hatchets/swords (+0.054) and daggers (+0.074) hold the **two smallest |loadings of all twelve variables** (ranks 12 and 10), while only house size (+0.327, rank 5) is materially present. The trio supplies **11.6% of PC2's sum of squares against 25% expected by chance**, and its PC2 range (0.2735) is **narrower than the economic group's (0.6426)** — so symbolic capital does not "spread across" PC2; it is compressed at zero there, with house size the single exception. PC1+PC2 absorb only **33%, 27% and 43%** of the three symbolic variables' variance — the **lowest communalities in the matrix** — and daggers turn out to be a **PC3 variable** (PC3 loading +0.593, the largest on that component; h² PC1–3 = 0.815).

## Stipulation 1 — sign convention, fixed before computation

Rule: *orient each component so its largest-|loading| variable is positive, ties broken by column order*; recorded before any eigendecomposition.

- **PC1 is set by `ZCU_AU` (Copper & Gold — social, +0.4072)** → **outside** the symbolic trio. No re-orientation was needed and none was done to flatter the contrast.
- PC2 is set by `ZBeil` (Axes & Celts — economic, +0.4706); PC3 is set by **`ZDolch` (symbolic, +0.5933)** — I flag this because a symbolic variable *does* orient a retained component, just not PC1 or PC2.
- The rule **flipped both PC1 and PC2** (all 12 raw signs reversed). Raw vs oriented, PC1/PC2:

| var | PC1 raw | PC1 oriented | PC2 raw | PC2 oriented |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZAxtSchwert | −0.2986 | **+0.2986** | −0.0540 | **+0.0540** |
| ZDolch | −0.2656 | **+0.2656** | −0.0742 | **+0.0742** |
| Zhausgr | −0.2251 | **+0.2251** | −0.3274 | **+0.3274** |
| ZCU_AU | −0.4072 | +0.4072 | −0.1867 | +0.1867 |
| Zamber | +0.2388 | −0.2388 | −0.4439 | +0.4439 |
| ZMonument | −0.2042 | +0.2042 | −0.2927 | +0.2927 |
| ZKeform | +0.3529 | −0.3529 | −0.3827 | +0.3827 |
| Zkeverz | −0.3821 | +0.3821 | −0.0674 | +0.0674 |
| ZHort | −0.3396 | +0.3396 | +0.1075 | −0.1075 |

| ZBeil | +0.2418 | −0.2418 | −0.4706 | +0.4706 |
| ZMW | −0.2417 | +0.2417 | −0.3914 | +0.3914 |

Mitigation: an alternative convention I checked (majority-positive) yields **identical oriented signs** for PC1 and PC2, and every claim about the trio below is a claim about magnitude, co-signing or rank — not about which pole is called positive.

## Stipulation 3 — variance table, then the PC1 characterisation

| comp | eigenvalue | PVE% | cum% |
|---|---|---|---|
| PC1 | 3.639 | **30.3** | 30.3 |
| PC2 | 2.336 | **19.5** | **49.8** |
| PC3 | 1.548 | 12.9 | 62.7 |
| PC4 | 1.500 | 12.5 | 75.2 |
| PC5 | 0.878 | 7.3 | 82.5 |
| PC6 | 0.744 | 6.2 | 88.7 |

**PC1 = 30.3%, PC2 = 19.5%, joint 49.8%** — the plane holds about half the variance, so a PC1/PC2 reading is defensible but not complete. PC1–PC4 all exceed broken-stick, but with median AR(1) **effective n ≈ 6.7 against a nominal 39** (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.44–0.91; 6–25 runs per series) the eigenvalues and any retention rule are optimistic, and the PC2/PC3 eigenvalue ratio is only 1.51, so PC2 is not a cleanly separated axis.

Full loading matrix (oriented; `r` = structure coefficient corr(var, PC); h² = variance absorbed):

| var | group | PC1 | r(PC1) | rank | PC2 | r(PC2) | rank | h² PC1+2 | h² PC1–3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZCU_AU | social | +0.4072 | +0.777 | 1 | +0.1867 | +0.285 | 7 | 0.685 | 0.698 |
| Zkeverz | cultural | +0.3821 | +0.729 | 2 | +0.0674 | +0.103 | 11 | 0.542 | 0.800 |
| ZKeform | cultural | −0.3529 | −0.673 | 3 | +0.3827 | +0.585 | 4 | **0.795** | 0.851 |
| ZHort | economic | +0.3396 | +0.648 | 4 | −0.1075 | −0.164 | 9 | 0.447 | 0.539 |
| **ZAxtSchwert** | **symbolic** | **+0.2986** | +0.570 | **5** | **+0.0540** | +0.082 | **12** | **0.331** | 0.337 |
| **ZDolch** | **symbolic** | **+0.2656** | +0.507 | **6** | **+0.0742** | +0.113 | **10** | **0.270** | 0.815 |
| ZBeil | economic | −0.2418 | −0.461 | 7 | +0.4706 | +0.719 | 1 | 0.730 | 0.733 |
| ZMW | economic | +0.2417 | +0.461 | 8 | +0.3914 | +0.598 | 3 | 0.570 | 0.615 |
| Zamber | social | −0.2388 | −0.456 | 9 | +0.4439 | +0.679 | 2 | 0.668 | 0.811 |
| **Zhausgr** | **symbolic** | **+0.2251** | +0.429 | **10** | **+0.3274** | +0.500 | **5** | **0.435** | 0.630 |
| ZMonument | social | +0.2042 | +0.390 | 11 | +0.2927 | +0.447 | 6 | 0.352 | 0.366 |
| ZSichel | economic | −0.1494 | −0.285 | 12 | −0.1720 | −0.263 | 8 | **0.150** | 0.327 |

**Position on PC1:** all three symbolic loadings are positive, sitting 0.03–0.18 below the top loading and inside the dominant positive pole — they are co-signed with Copper&Gold, Pottery Decoration and Depot, and opposite to Pottery Form, Amber, Axes&Celts and Sickle. Mean |PC1| for the trio is 0.263 vs 0.279 for all variables (**3rd of 4 groups**), i.e. ordinary, not defining. **What PC1 contrasts is time, not capital forms:** the correlation between the PC1 loading vector and each variable's own correlation with year is **r = 0.959**, PC1 scores correlate **r = +0.82 with calendar year**, and mean PC1 by period runs EN −1.74, MN −1.37, SG −1.12, LN +0.33, YBA +1.85, OBA +3.09. PC1 is a general "rising-toward-the-Bronze-Age" axis on which symbolic capital participates moderately; the PC1 split is not symbolic-vs-economic (economic and cultural each straddle zero, ranges 0.58 and 0.74) — and PC1 explains 32%/26%/18% of the trio's variance, so most of what makes them symbolic is *not* on PC1.

## Stipulation 2 — PC2 spread, quantified and made comparative

| var | PC2 loading | abs | rank | h² PC1+2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZAxtSchwert | +0.0540 | 0.0540 | **12 / 12** | 0.331 |
| ZDolch | +0.0742 | 0.0742 | **10 / 12** | 0.270 |
| Zhausgr | +0.3274 | 0.3274 | **5 / 12** | 0.435 |

- **Same side or straddling?** All three **share the positive side** — they do **not** straddle zero. But the agreement is carried by house size: the two weapons are within 0.02 of zero.
- **Within-symbolic PC2 range = 0.2735.** Contrasts: **economic 0.6426** (4 vars, largest group, spans zero: −0.172 to +0.471), **social 0.2572** (all positive), **cultural 0.3153**. So symbolic spread on PC2 is **~2.3× narrower than economic**, slightly *wider* than social, narrower than cultural — comparative, and the honest reading is "moderate range with two near-zero members", not "widely distributed".
- **Group share of PC2's eigenvector sum-of-squares (uniform expectation in brackets):** symbolic **11.6%** [25.0], social 31.8% [25.0], cultural 15.1% [16.7], economic **41.6%** [33.3]. Symbolic capital is **under-represented on PC2 by half**; PC2's real poles are Axes&Celts/Amber/Monument Size/Pottery Form vs Sickle/Depot, and it correlates **r = +0.747 with the mean of all standardised Z but r = −0.07 with time** — PC2 is a "how much capital overall" axis, which the symbolic weapons mostly ignore.
- **Communalities confirm the trio is the least well described by this plane** (0.331 / 0.270 / 0.435, the three lowest of the twelve except Sickle 0.150); adding PC3 lifts daggers 0.27 → 0.815 and house size 0.435 → 0.630.

## Stipulation 4 — both sensitivity checks; does the story flip?

**A. 37-slice subset (CE −4100…−500, the grid shared with `time_series_data.csv`).** PC1 32.4%, PC2 16.4%, joint 48.9%. PC1 here is oriented by **`ZKeform` (cultural, +0.4087)**, so the convention reverses the whole PC1 vector — trio oriented PC1 becomes **−0.2764 / −0.2316 / −0.1703** (ranks 7, 9, 10), **negative**. Sign-invariant check: PC1 loading vectors correlate **r = −0.9957**, i.e. **the identical axis**; trio PC2 stays positive (**+0.1413 / +0.2013 / +0.3648**, ranks 11, 7, 3, range 0.2235). So the *substantive* trio characterisation (co-signed mid-pack on PC1; two weapons near zero, house size non-trivial on PC2) **does not flip** — but the **sign does, purely as a convention artefact**, and PC2's loading vector only correlates **r = +0.77** with the main run's PC2 (PC2/PC3 swap partly), so PC2's identity is the least stable quantity here.

**B. Covariance matrix (no re-standardisation).** PC1 31.8%, PC2 20.4%, joint 52.3%. PC1 vectors correlate **r = +0.9948**, PC2 **r = +0.9908** — the axes are essentially unchanged. Trio PC1 **+0.3010 / +0.2793 / +0.2283** (ranks 5, 6, 10 — identical ranks), range 0.0727; trio PC2 **+0.0666 / +0.1195 / +0.3644** (ranks 11, 8, 5), all positive, range 0.2978 vs economic 0.5363. **The symbolic characterisation does NOT flip under covariance.** ZSichel's SD is therefore *not* the crux for this question — what the scaling basis actually changes is the **economic contrast group**: Sickle collapses from (−0.149, −0.172; h² 0.150) to (−0.062, −0.059; h² **0.022**), i.e. under covariance it is effectively removed from both components. So the conditional-scaling statement should be filed honestly as: *the symbolic-trio answer is robust to the correlation-vs-covariance choice; the economic-group contrast used to define what PC2 "means" is the part that is scaling-conditional.*

**Block bootstrap (circular, block = 5 centuries, B = 2000, sign-aligned), next to the eigenvalues:** P(PC1 > 0) = 0.972 / 0.950 / 0.844 and P(all three co-signed on PC1) = **0.837** — co-signing on PC1 is the sturdiest result, though the 95% intervals still touch zero (ZAxtSchwert −0.001…+0.539). On PC2, P(PC2 > 0) = **0.560 / 0.596 / 0.756** and P(all three co-signed) = **0.591** — barely better than a coin flip, so "the three symbolic components share the same side of PC2" is a point estimate, not a demonstrated pattern; the symbolic PC2 range is median 0.300 [0.047, 0.796] vs economic 0.672 [0.302, 1.010], overlapping.

## Plain-language hypothesis (the deliverable)

In the 100-year-slice PCA of forms of capital (39 slices, 12 standardised indicators, correlation matrix; PC1 30%, PC2 20%, jointly 50% of variance), the symbolic-capital components — house size, daggers, hatchets/swords — **load on PC1 with the same sign and closely similar moderate magnitude (oriented +0.23 to +0.30, ranks 5–10 of 12, the tightest group on that axis), placing them inside PC1's dominant pole alongside copper/gold, pottery decoration and hoards rather than opposing it**; PC1 is best read as a temporal "general rise of capital" axis (loading vector vs per-variable time trend r = 0.96) rather than as a contest between capital forms, so symbolic capital is characterised as *following* the main trend rather than defining it. On PC2 the trio **does not distribute widely**: all three lie on the same (positive) side of zero, but hatchets/swords and daggers carry the two smallest loadings in the entire matrix (rank 12 and 10) and only house size registers (rank 5), with a within-symbolic spread (0.27) less than half the economic group's (0.64) and a share of PC2 variance (11.6%) under half of chance expectation (25%). Symbolic capital is therefore **concentrated on PC1 and largely orthogonal to PC2**, with the weapons' distinctive information residing on PC3 (daggers are PC3's largest loading) — which is also why PC1+PC2 explain only 27–43% of the three symbolic variables, the weakest communalities in the analysis. Caveats that survive reproduction: component signs are convention-dependent and flip under the 37-slice subset while the underlying axes do not (|cos| = 0.996); PC2's identity itself is unstable (r = 0.77 across subsets); and with lag-1 autocorrelation 0.44–0.91 the effective number of independent century-slices is ~7, so none of the PC2-level claims should be treated as significant.

**One pollen flag, not pursued here:** PC1 correlates +0.82 with calendar year, so any capital↔Belau openness association would be dominated by shared trend unless detrended — worth a separate piece of work.

Reproducibility: `analysis/05_final_capital_pca.py` regenerates everything end to end (self-contained, fixed 100-yr input, fixed pre-declared sign rule, both sensitivities); `analysis/01_inspect_capital_inputs.py` reproduces all the data facts from stage 1; `analysis/03_stability_and_spread.py` reproduces the bootstrap and broken-stick numbers; `analysis/capital_pca_summary.txt` plus four CSVs hold the tables.

payload.hypothesis: In a PCA of twelve forms of capital over 39 hundred-year slices (correlation matrix; PC1 = 30.3%, PC2 = 19.5%, jointly 49.8% of variance), the symbolic-capital components - house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) - load on PC1 with one shared sign and closely similar moderate magnitude (oriented +0.23 to +0.30; ranks 5, 6 and 10 of 12; within-group range 0.07, the tightest of any capital form), i.e. they sit inside PC1's dominant pole together with copper/gold, pottery decoration and hoards rather than opposing it, and add nothing to it: PC1 behaves as a general temporal rise of capital (loading vector vs per-variable time trend r = 0.96), so symbolic capital follows the main axis instead of defining or contesting it. On PC2 the trio does NOT spread widely: although all three nominally share the positive side of zero, hatchets/swords (+0.054) and daggers (+0.074) carry the two smallest loadings in the whole matrix (ranks 12 and 10) and only house size (+0.327, rank 5) registers, giving a within-symbolic PC2 range of 0.27, less than half the economic group's 0.64, and a share of PC2's variance (11.6%) under half of the 25% expected by chance. Symbolic capital is therefore concentrated on PC1 and essentially orthogonal to PC2, and it is the least well represented group in the PC1-PC2 plane (communalities 0.27-0.43, the weakest after sickle), with the weapons' distinctive information falling on PC3 (daggers are PC3's largest loading, +0.59). Caveats: signs are convention-dependent (the 37-slice subset flips PC1's sign but not the axis, |cos| = 0.996), PC2's identity is unstable (loading agreement r = 0.77 across subsets; PC2/PC3 eigenvalue ratio 1.51), the covariance-matrix run leaves the symbolic characterisation unchanged (r = 0.99) but erases sickle from the economic contrast, and with stepped series the effective n is about 7 rather than 39, so PC2-level claims are not statistically secure.
payload.workflow: 1) Load capital.csv with decimal=',' (comma decimal separators), index by CE = -BCE, drop BCE/group/color -> complete 39 x 12 matrix of 100-yr slices. 2) Declare sign convention (orient on largest-|loading| variable, ties by column order) before computing. 3) PCA by eigendecomposition of the 12x12 correlation matrix (columns re-standardised on the 39 slices), all 12 components retained; eigenvector loadings, structure coefficients r = v*sqrt(eigenvalue), communalities, |loading| ranks. 4) Group spread summaries (range, same-side test, share of eigenvector sum-of-squares vs n/12 expectation). 5) Sensitivity A: 37-slice subset shared with time_series_data.csv; Sensitivity B: covariance matrix without re-standardisation; both compared with sign-invariant r on loading vectors. 6) Circular block bootstrap (block = 5 centuries, B = 2000, sign-aligned to the observed loadings) for loading intervals, sign probabilities and group-range distributions; broken-stick comparison; AR(1) effective-n diagnostics for the stepped series. 7) Axis-meaning diagnostics: PC scores vs calendar year, vs mean of all standardised Z, and by archaeological period; PC3 inspection for the trio. Pollen openness deliberately excluded.
